findings.claim: The archived LCME test suite collected 29 tests under the current isolated replay. Fourteen dependency-independent tests passed. Fifteen failed or cascaded because sentence_transformers is unavailable in the replay environment; pyproject.toml declares sentence-transformers>=2.2.0 as a required dependency, so those failures are environment blockers rather than demonstrated LCME semantic failures.
findings.implication: Reuse the 14 dependency-independent tests immediately and re-run the full 29 under a frozen environment that satisfies the archived dependency contract before assigning current PASS/FAIL.

findings.claim: Historical LCME baseline results report p50 retrieval around 11.7-12.4ms and p95 13.9-15.8ms for 100-1000 memories with MRR 0.967-1.0. Extended results report Recall@5 0.96, nDCG@5 0.978, 8.8 writes/s, zero errors in a 100-writer/90-reader concurrent run, contradiction success 7/10, and 200-turn early-fact P@1 0.75/P@5 0.875/MRR 0.792.
findings.implication: Use these as historical reference bands and weakness targets, never as current performance claims; current ClayGraph/UnifiedDB must replicate under matched corpora/hardware and report tail latency plus accuracy/failure cases.

findings.claim: The extended benchmark's manual_forget_works=false result is not a valid product-failure oracle: immediately after ingest it selects only type='memory' AND protected=0, while ingestion.py deliberately creates new memory chunks protected=True with an unprotect_after timestamp 24 hours later. In the normal benchmark state no candidate exists, so forget() is not actually exercised.
findings.implication: Correct the forgetting fixture before reuse: explicitly unprotect/age a known memory and assert both forget-success and protected-forget rejection. Treat benchmark logic itself as testable artifact with provenance/version.

findings.claim: The archive implements tri-hybrid SQLite + vector + graph storage, FTS/vector dual-path retrieval, RRF/recency/confidence ranking, claim-not-fact ingestion, protected-memory lifecycle, neural cold-start fallbacks and consolidation. These mechanisms substantially overlap the already mapped Project-Frankenstein LCME lineage.
findings.implication: Consume as executable/source corroboration and test oracle, not as independent architecture replication or additional earned-work credit.

findings.claim: The historical extended corpus exposes unresolved quality ceilings: contradiction update retrieval succeeds only 70%, and after 200 turns early-fact retrieval is 75% top-1 / 87.5% top-5. These are stronger design targets than the near-perfect small baseline aggregate.
findings.implication: Mandatory current retrieval evaluation should include temporal supersession/contradiction cases and long-horizon early-fact recovery, not only random retrieval averages.

branch_feedback.unifieddb: Import contradiction/supersession and corrected forgetting fixtures; compare exact/FTS/vector/graph store roles under matched corpus and preserve physical-isolation decisions separately from semantic identity.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Use the 70% contradiction and 200-turn retrieval weaknesses to test temporal/provenance/conflict semantics and graph expansion; do not assume graph presence solves supersession.
branch_feedback.harness: Add benchmark-oracle validation itself as a gate: fixture preconditions must be asserted before interpreting failures. Re-run all 29 archived tests with dependencies frozen and classify environment vs semantic failures.
branch_feedback.frank: LCME source corroborates historical memory architecture but does not restore it wholesale; current memory authority/provenance rules outrank old package defaults.

earned_work_reason: Hybrid LCME retrieval/fallback architecture already has historical earned-work mapping. This run contributes execution/benchmark-quality oracles only and deliberately avoids duplicate credit.
